messages.text: The interval’s own constructor invariant is violated when start is not before end.
A well-formed interval says nothing about whether the meter is free.
The schedule can change after the constructor check, so commit must recheck overlap.
Silently swapping endpoints changes the submitted interval instead of rejecting invalid input.

feedback.reason: The interval’s own validity is local, while overlap depends on changing schedule state; the prompt assigns them different checks.

options.text: Defer start/end validation until a meter is physically committed.
Treat any valid interval value as proof the meter is free.
Query schedule overlap in the interval constructor and assume it cannot change.
Accept reversed endpoints and normalize them by swapping without user intent.
Validate start < end on interval creation; check overlap at commit.

questions.prompt: In a neighborhood energy-sharing service, the meter operator must reserve a discharge window. A meter cannot be committed twice for an overlapping window. A reservation window is a value with start and end instants; its constructor must reject start >= end. Whether another reservation overlaps is checked against the current schedule when committing. Which split respects both rules?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A well-formed compatible configuration does not guarantee the provider will be reachable or that the later switch succeeds.
details.errorCorrection: An endpoint string alone cannot establish language or timing compatibility; matching one field does not satisfy the conjunction.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The provider configuration is valid only when its supplied provider supports both the stream language and timing mode and carries the required public error contract.
details.scenarioApplication: The factory compares the candidate’s declared support with the stream’s language/timing inputs and records the unchanged outward error contract before the switch is attempted.
details.transfer: Validate compatibility from all named inputs, then leave runtime availability and execution success to the operation that uses the configuration.

messages.text: An endpoint alone cannot establish the language/timing support required before the switch.
Different caller mappings would break the preserved stream-facing error contract.
The prompt specifically requires supported language and timing; universal support is contradicted.
Passing through provider-specific errors changes the public stream contract.

feedback.reason: The configuration needs enough facts to check the stated compatibility, while preserving the stream-facing contract across provider changes.

options.text: Assume every provider supports every language and timing mode.
Replace the stream’s error contract with the provider’s raw errors.
Create config only for supported language/timing; retain the stream’s public error contract.
Construct a provider config from an endpoint alone and discover language incompatibility on the first caption.
Let each caller invent a different error mapping after the switch.

questions.prompt: In a live captioning studio, the caption supervisor must switch the active language provider. The current stream keeps its timing and error contract. A stream switch requires a provider that supports the stream language and timing mode. The new provider configuration must retain the existing stream’s public error contract. What should the factory produce?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A request with distinct IDs is syntactically valid, not a promise that both assignments remain eligible when the swap commits.
details.errorCorrection: Checking availability only at request creation can become stale; accepting duplicate IDs fails to describe two distinct assignments.
details.mechanismOrProperty: SwapRequest is locally invalid when its two assignment IDs are identical. Skill and availability are mutable facts that the prompt assigns to the later swap operation.
details.scenarioApplication: Construction rejects a self-swap before execution; at commit the operation reloads current assignment facts and checks both volunteers’ skills and availability.
details.transfer: Validate request-internal relations at creation and recheck changing eligibility at execution.

messages.text: A swap with the same ID twice does not satisfy the two-distinct-assignment request.
Availability can change before execution, so a constructor-time result can be stale.
Creating replacement assignments before validating the request can create effects for an invalid swap.
Assignment construction cannot establish current availability of both volunteers.

feedback.reason: Distinct IDs are an invariant of the request value; live availability is time-sensitive and belongs to the later operation as stated.

options.text: Reject identical assignment IDs; recheck current skills and availability at execution.
Allow identical IDs and treat the request as a no-op swap.
Query current availability in the request constructor and trust it at a later commit.
Create replacement assignments before checking the request has two distinct IDs.
Make assignment construction itself enforce both volunteers’ current availability.

questions.prompt: In a volunteer coordination hub, the shift manager must swap two volunteer assignments. Skills and availability constraints hold for both assignments. A swap request contains two distinct assignment IDs. Skill and availability can change before execution, so the swap operation rechecks them at commit. What should request creation enforce?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A recorded parent proves the edit’s ancestry, not that it can be merged or that its branch will be accepted.
details.errorCorrection: Without a parent ID, review cannot identify the edit’s base; applying it directly to the latest route would lose the explicit branch boundary.
details.mechanismOrProperty: An edit must carry its parent revision ID so later conflict logic can compare the branch with the route’s current revision.
details.scenarioApplication: The factory records which revision the offline edit began from. If the route advances, acceptance retains the edit as a branch for review rather than overwriting newer geometry.
details.transfer: Capture the reference needed to detect later divergence, then resolve mutable current-state conflicts at acceptance.

messages.text: Without the parent ID, conflict review cannot tell which route revision the edit branched from.
Discarding a stale branch contradicts the explicit retention requirement.
Applying during construction overwrites current route state before acceptance.
Substituting current geometry erases the submitted branch rather than retaining it.

feedback.reason: Capturing the parent lets later review identify the base of the branch without silently replacing a newer accepted route.

options.text: Reject any edit whose parent is not current, discarding the submitted branch.
Apply the edit to the current route during construction.
Replace missing geometry with the accepted route’s current geometry.
Require the parent revision ID; retain a branch and compare it at acceptance.
Construct an edit without a parent and attach whichever revision is latest when submitted.

questions.prompt: In a local-first map editor, the cartographer must merge an offline route edit. Conflicts are explicit and never silently overwrite accepted geometry. An edit must identify its parent route revision. If the current route revision has advanced, the submission is still retained as a branch for explicit conflict review; it must never overwrite the newer route. What should the edit factory capture?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A later campaign revision can govern future claims but does not rewrite the revision recorded by an already-created claim.
details.errorCorrection: Creating a claim before eligibility is established records a reward the scenario does not authorize.
details.mechanismOrProperty: RewardClaim requires a prior eligible result tied to the character and campaign revision. The revision makes the rule context for this claim explicit.
details.scenarioApplication: The factory receives the eligibility result and its campaign revision; it does not infer eligibility from current quest fields or mutate them to make a claim possible.
details.transfer: Construct downstream records from an explicit decision and the exact context that decision evaluated.

messages.text: Recording the reward before checking eligibility creates a claim the prompt forbids.
Changing quest state inside construction does not establish the required prior eligible result.
Without the revision, the claim cannot say which campaign rules produced eligibility.
A later rules revision must not retroactively change the eligibility basis of this claim.

feedback.reason: The prompt makes the eligibility result and rule revision prerequisites to the claim; claim creation must not invent the result or rewrite quest state.

options.text: Recompute against future campaign rules whenever an old claim is viewed.
Require the eligibility result and campaign revision before claim creation.
Construct a claim from character ID alone and check eligibility after recording the reward.
Let the claim constructor change quest state to make the reward eligible.
Store “eligible” without the campaign revision used to determine it.

questions.prompt: In a board-game campaign manager, the campaign host must apply a reward to a character. Reward rules depend on the current legal campaign state. A reward claim can be created only after the campaign rules produce an eligible result for the current character and campaign revision. The claim stores that revision. What should claim creation require?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A valid assignment reflects the recorded capability and acknowledgement; the factory cannot manufacture carrier acceptance or promise later operational performance.
details.errorCorrection: Temperature compatibility alone says nothing about custody transfer; a capability match cannot stand in for the second required fact.
details.mechanismOrProperty: CarrierAssignment requires two independent supplied facts: the carrier covers the shipment’s temperature band, and custody handoff is acknowledged. Both are present in the carrier acceptance record.
details.scenarioApplication: The factory checks the accepted carrier record against the shipment band and requires its custody acknowledgement before producing the new assignment.
details.transfer: When a valid object depends on multiple independent facts, verify each one from its named source before construction.

messages.text: Temperature compatibility alone does not satisfy the separate custody acknowledgement condition.
Custody acknowledgement alone says nothing about temperature compatibility.
Missing either acceptance fact permits an invalid assignment object to be created.
Changing the carrier before evidence exists reverses the required order.

feedback.reason: Both requirements define a valid accepted assignment; checking only one can create a value that the prompt forbids.

options.text: Create the reassignment after checking temperature but before custody is acknowledged.
Treat custody acknowledgement alone as proof of temperature compatibility.
Construct an assignment with missing acceptance facts and let dispatch screens infer them.
Change the shipment carrier first and collect evidence afterward.
Require compatible temperature band and custody acknowledgement before reassignment.

questions.prompt: In a cold-chain logistics console, the dispatch planner must reassign a shipment to a carrier. Temperature restrictions and hand-off ownership travel with the shipment. A carrier assignment is valid only when its temperature capability covers the shipment band and custody has been acknowledged. The carrier’s acceptance record contains both facts. What should the reassignment factory accept?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This validates the proposal against its stated snapshot but does not guarantee commit success or reserve funds.
details.errorCorrection: A locally valid allocation can become too large after another charge; construction alone cannot reserve the snapshot balance.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The allocation’s local rule is 0 < amount <= supplied balance snapshot. The account’s current balance may change before posting.
details.scenarioApplication: Construction validates the proposed amount against the snapshot passed with it; posting reloads the ledger balance and repeats the current-balance guard.
details.transfer: Bind a draft calculation to its observed snapshot, then recheck mutable balances when applying it.

messages.text: Zero or negative amount violates the allocation’s local value invariant.
A snapshot only validates the proposed amount against that earlier balance; the current balance can differ at posting.
Hiding the balance snapshot prevents the proposed value from recording which check it passed.
Clamping silently changes the requested amount rather than validating it.

feedback.reason: The local allocation value must satisfy the supplied snapshot rule, but the prompt explicitly says posting needs a fresh check.

options.text: Read the live balance in the amount constructor and hide which snapshot was used.
Clamp an oversized amount to whatever balance is available.
Validate amount against the supplied balance snapshot; recheck current balance at posting.
Allow zero or negative allocations and rely on the ledger to repair them.
Treat a valid snapshot check as a guarantee the balance will still be sufficient at posting.

questions.prompt: In a cooperative lending ledger, the account steward must record a repayment allocation. A repayment cannot reduce the outstanding balance below zero. An allocation amount must be positive and no greater than the balance snapshot used at creation. The balance may change before posting, so the ledger rechecks the current balance at commit. Where do the two checks belong?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: The decision can be constructed only from the stated active/elapsed facts; commit still decides against current match state.
details.errorCorrection: A UI-only timeout check misses other callers, while trusting a once-valid decision after another process finalizes the match uses stale state.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Forfeit eligibility combines a currently active match and an elapsed timeout. Match state and clock passage can change between decision construction and commit.
details.scenarioApplication: The decision path checks both facts when forming the forfeit decision and checks active state again when committing; a match finalized in between cannot be advanced by stale eligibility.
details.transfer: Validate observed eligibility for the proposed action, but recheck mutable state at the effect boundary.

messages.text: A UI-only check leaves other callers able to create an invalid forfeit decision.
The match may finalize before commit, so the stale active flag is insufficient.
Timeout elapsed alone does not override a match that has since finalized.
Advancing the bracket is an effect after eligibility, not a constructor side effect.

feedback.reason: Eligibility depends on current match state and time, so creation must check the stated rule and commit must not trust an obsolete state.

options.text: Check active match and elapsed timeout, then recheck match state at commit.
Construct a forfeit for any match and validate only in the user interface.
Create a forfeit based on a stale “active” flag and skip the commit-time check.
Allow a forfeit after a match is finalized because timeout once elapsed.
Let the forfeit constructor advance the bracket before confirming match eligibility.

questions.prompt: In a tournament bracket service, the match official must forfeit a match after a timeout. The bracket advances only from a legal match state. A forfeit decision may be created only for an active match after its timeout has elapsed. The match can be finalized by another process before this decision is committed. What should the domain API do?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This rule constrains category membership only; the prompt does not say a submitted category can never be corrected or prescribe refund results.
details.errorCorrection: An arbitrary category bypasses the listed set, and “refund pending” mixes a later policy outcome into an inspection classification.
details.mechanismOrProperty: ConditionReport accepts one of the inspection categories listed by its domain and contains no refund outcome. RefundPolicy consumes the report later.
details.scenarioApplication: The constructor accepts an inspection category; it does not accept refund language as a category or try to evaluate refund policy before the report exists.
details.transfer: Keep a classification within its stated vocabulary and separate it from downstream decisions that consume it.

messages.text: An arbitrary category bypasses the prompt’s allowed category set.
The prompt excludes refund eligibility from this report and supplies no policy for it.
A condition report can be created before the separate refund decision.
“Refund pending” is a downstream policy outcome, not one of the inspection categories the report is allowed to carry.

feedback.reason: The listed category set is the report’s local validity rule; refund eligibility is expressly a separate later decision.

options.text: Set refund eligibility in the report constructor using an unstated policy.
Reject report creation unless a refund has already been decided.
Use a refund outcome such as “refund pending” as the condition category, although it is not an inspection category.
Create only from an allowed condition category; do not store the later refund outcome.
Allow arbitrary category strings and normalize them after submission.

questions.prompt: In a returns inspection workflow, the warehouse inspector must classify a returned item. Classification and refund eligibility are not the same responsibility. A condition report accepts only one of the listed inspection categories and does not include refund eligibility. Refund policy consumes the report later. What should report construction enforce?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This factory validates run outcome and output presence; it does not make the run succeed or define how it was executed.
details.errorCorrection: A run ID alone does not establish success, and publishing a placeholder before output exists creates a result the prompt says is not ready.
details.mechanismOrProperty: PublishedResult can contain only a terminal output from a succeeded run. A queued/running run has no final output, and a failed run has diagnostics of a different kind.
details.scenarioApplication: The factory requires both succeeded state and terminal output before constructing PublishedResult; failure diagnostics stay in their separate failure record.
details.transfer: Require the completed product of an operation before constructing a record that represents that product as final.

messages.text: A queued or running execution has not produced the terminal output required for publication.
Failure diagnostics explain a failed run; they are not its successful published output.
Publishing before the final output exists creates the result record the factory is meant to prevent.
A run ID alone does not establish success or provide a terminal output.

feedback.reason: Only a succeeded run has the final output the prompt permits a PublishedResult to store; diagnostics from a failed run have a different record type.

options.text: Construct a PublishedResult from any run ID, even if the run failed or has no output.
Require a succeeded run and its terminal output before constructing PublishedResult.
Allow a queued or running run and replace the published output when execution finishes.
Treat failure diagnostics as the terminal output of a successful result.
Publish a result record before output exists and attach the output later.

questions.prompt: In a research-notebook platform, a run can be queued, running, succeeded, or failed. Only a succeeded run has a terminal output eligible for publication; a failed run has diagnostics instead. A PublishedResult stores the final output, while failed-run diagnostics use a separate record. What should the result factory require?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If this operation required a reservation to transfer, confirmed absence could be a command-level not-found outcome. This operation is the preceding read.
details.errorCorrection: No reservation is expected for many plots; outage is not another spelling of absence.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Returning no reservation is a successful lookup result. A database outage means the lookup did not establish whether one exists, so its failure must remain observable.
details.scenarioApplication: The plot steward needs three distinguishable observations here: a reservation, a confirmed absence, or an unsuccessful read.
details.transfer: For reads with expected missing records, preserve absence as data and preserve inability to read as failure.

messages.text: The empty option is a normal value; an outage is an operation failure.
An empty reservation object would claim that a reservation exists after the lookup confirmed none.
Not found and failed lookup call for different caller behavior.
The plot itself does not encode whether the lookup succeeded.

feedback.reason: No current reservation is an expected empty result, while a database outage is a failed lookup; the contract must not collapse those cases.

options.text: Return absent reservation as a normal optional result; return lookup failure separately.
Return null for both no reservation and database failure.
Return an empty reservation object when none exists.
Throw the same “not found” error for no reservation and storage outage.
Make callers query a plot field to infer whether a reservation was returned.

questions.prompt: In a community garden allocation tool, the plot steward must transfer a plot reservation. Transfer preserves the plot boundary and approval history. A plot reservation lookup is a read: many plots have no current reservation, and that is normal. A database outage must still be reported separately. What should the lookup contract express?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a component were optional, the prompt would need to say how omission affects the quote. Here every required component price is needed.
details.errorCorrection: Use the missing component identity to distinguish incomplete pricing input from a valid numeric total.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Zero belongs to the quote domain. A missing component price prevents calculation and must identify which required input is unavailable.
details.scenarioApplication: The bundle may total zero even though every component price is present; a missing component price is a different condition and blocks a quote.
details.transfer: Never reserve an otherwise valid numeric value as a marker for missing input when the prompt allows that value.

messages.text: The prompt separates a valid numeric value from unavailable pricing input.
An optional quote alone cannot explain which required price is missing.
Previous regional prices are not an authorized substitute.
The caller needs the missing component to repair the quote request.

feedback.reason: Zero is a valid quote total under the prompt; missing required input is an error with actionable component context.

options.text: Return no quote for both a valid zero total and a missing component price.
Fill missing component prices from the previous regional quote.
Throw an untyped error that does not identify the missing component.
Return a valid quote, including zero, or a missing-component-price error.
Use zero to mean a component price was not found.

questions.prompt: In a subscription packaging service, the catalog manager must add a regional bundle. The bundle pricing policy remains consistent with its components. A regional bundle quote may have a valid total of zero. If any required component price is missing, the quote cannot be calculated and the missing component must be named. What should the quote operation return?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An optional charger plus a distinct read error could encode the same meanings. The important contract is that the two outcomes remain distinguishable.
details.errorCorrection: An empty search and an unreadable search are different results: only the first justifies showing “none available.”
details.mechanismOrProperty: No matching charger is a completed search result; a failed schedule read leaves availability unknown. The caller needs “none available” only after the schedule was read.
details.scenarioApplication: The result must preserve whether a charger was found, the search completed with no match, or the store could not answer.
details.transfer: Only report a negative search result when the source needed to establish it was read successfully.

messages.text: The fact that no charger is available is not itself a storage error.
A schedule timeout did not confirm an empty search, so this would falsely tell the operator that no charger is available.
A charger that is already occupied does not satisfy the search for a free charger.
A failed read cannot establish that no charger matches.

feedback.reason: The caller takes different actions for normal unavailability and failed schedule access, so both need distinct outcome cases.

options.text: Return “no charger” for both an empty schedule and a failed schedule read.
Use separate outcomes for available, no match, and schedule-read failure.
Return an empty charger object for both no match and store failure.
Return no match when the schedule read fails, so the caller reports “none available.”
Return the first charger even when it is occupied.

questions.prompt: In a fleet charging coordinator, the station operator must reserve a charger. Charger capacity and reservation expiry are coordinated. A charger search can find no free charger, and callers should show “none available.” If the schedule store cannot be read, callers should offer retry. How should search outcomes be represented?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the archive later defines absent and blank captions as equivalent, normalization could be valid; the current contract expressly keeps them distinct.
details.errorCorrection: Normalizing absence to empty loses whether the curator intentionally chose blank text.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Caption presence carries curator intent independently from the string contents: absent metadata differs from a stored empty string.
details.scenarioApplication: The field must carry both whether caption metadata was supplied and, when present, its text.
details.transfer: When an empty value is meaningful, model presence separately from the contained value.

messages.text: The presence bit matters independently of the caption’s string contents.
One null value cannot distinguish the two meanings the prompt defines.
A placeholder creates content the curator never supplied.
An explicitly stored empty value must remain present under this contract.

feedback.reason: The two states carry different curator intent; collapsing absence into empty text loses that distinction.

options.text: Normalize absent metadata to an empty string.
Use null for both missing metadata and intentionally blank caption.
Make caption required and invent placeholder text when it is absent.
Drop empty captions during serialization because they display no characters.
Represent caption as optional text so absent differs from stored empty.

questions.prompt: In a photo-archive curation tool, the archivist must merge duplicate metadata. Asset identity remains stable while descriptive values are replaced. An archived photo may have no caption metadata, while an explicitly stored empty caption means the curator intentionally chose blank text. How should the metadata field be modeled?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If policy introduced a default, it would have to be stated as a rule. The prompt instead makes both fields mandatory.
details.errorCorrection: Field-specific validation identifies the missing territory or expiry without inventing a default license scope.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The request can parse while required territory or expiry is absent. Validation should report the specific missing field before any clearance lookup or approval.
details.scenarioApplication: The analyst must know which of the two mandatory inputs to repair; neither a broad false value nor a search result supplies that guidance.
details.transfer: Keep malformed request input distinct from a valid request that returns no matching record.

messages.text: The prompt supplies no worldwide scope or permanent duration, so these defaults would authorize more than the request states.
An empty accepted clearance would report success despite a missing mandatory field.
A boolean cannot provide the repair details the prompt requires.
No matching clearance is a result after valid input is searched, not a substitute for missing input.

feedback.reason: Missing required input is a malformed request, not a valid global/permanent clearance or a search miss.

options.text: Use one generic false result that does not identify which field is missing.
Represent either missing field as “no matching clearance.”
Return field-specific validation errors for missing territory or expiry.
Treat missing territory as worldwide and missing expiry as permanent.
Return an empty clearance as though a request was accepted.

questions.prompt: In a digital rights clearance tool, the licensing analyst must approve a territory-specific usage. Approval requires an explicit territory and expiration. Territory and expiry are mandatory for clearance. The request can be syntactically parsed while either field is missing; the analyst must receive field-specific repair guidance. What should request validation return?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: An availability-only search could filter assigned batteries if that behavior were explicitly requested. This lookup is required to distinguish the two cases.
details.errorCorrection: Reporting “not found” for an assigned battery erases a fact the caller needs; returning an unassigned battery fabricates state.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The serial lookup has an existence question and, for a found battery, an assignment-state question. A known assigned battery is not a missing record.
details.scenarioApplication: The coordinator needs to tell the operator whether the serial identifies a battery and whether that battery is currently assignable.
details.transfer: Do not collapse a present record that fails a requested condition into record absence.

messages.text: The query has an absence state and a found state with a separate assignment condition.
The prompt explicitly distinguishes no record from a record that cannot be scheduled.
Null can represent an unknown serial, but omitting assignment status hides whether a found battery is already assigned.
Assigned is an expected domain condition, not necessarily a system failure.

feedback.reason: The record exists in the assigned case, so it must not be reported as absent; callers also need to know whether the requested serial exists.

options.text: Report unknown serial separately from a found-but-assigned battery.
Return “not found” for both conditions.
Return an unassigned battery even when the serial is unknown.
Use null for an unknown serial and omit assignment status for found batteries.
Return a generic error whenever a battery is assigned.

questions.prompt: In a drone maintenance planner, the fleet coordinator must schedule a battery replacement. A battery cannot be assigned to two aircraft at once. Battery search uses a serial number. An unknown serial means no battery record; a known battery already assigned to an aircraft is a different condition. What should the lookup report?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A UI may render both non-granted states similarly, but any representation is acceptable if it preserves their distinction and keeps both from authorizing send.
details.errorCorrection: Mapping denied and not-recorded to one null outcome loses a distinction the prompt explicitly requires; treating every existing record as permission would authorize a denied referral.
details.mechanismOrProperty: The scenario defines three completed lookup values plus an independent possibility that a lookup operation cannot complete. The contract must distinguish the three values without prescribing enum, tagged-union, or nullable encoding.
details.scenarioApplication: Not recorded, denied, and granted remain separately observable; the send path permits disclosure only from the granted outcome.
details.transfer: Specify the observable states and allowed action first; choose any encoding that preserves them without changing policy.

messages.text: An existing record may be explicitly denied; record presence alone does not authorize disclosure.
This maps denied and not-recorded to the same result, although the prompt requires both states to remain distinguishable.
The stated rule permits sending only for granted consent; missing evidence is not a grant.
The lookup succeeded and returned a valid not-recorded state, so this is not an operational failure.

feedback.reason: The contract must preserve the three states stated in the prompt and permit external sending only for granted consent; no particular programming-language representation is required.

options.text: Return granted as true and collapse denied and not recorded into one null result.
Treat the absence of a consent record as permission unless a denial is stored.
Preserve not-recorded, denied, and granted as distinct outcomes; allow sending only for granted.
Treat any existing consent record, including an explicit denial, as permission to send.
Report not-recorded as a transport failure even when the lookup completed successfully.

questions.prompt: In a clinic referral coordinator, the care navigator must route a referral to a specialist. Privacy and consent rules apply before external disclosure. Consent lookup has three possible outcomes: not recorded, explicitly denied, and granted. The referral caller must distinguish not-recorded from denied for its follow-up action. A referral may be sent only for granted consent. What result contract preserves these requirements?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If timeout attempts could earn partial credit, the policy would need to define that combination; this prompt says no answer means no score.
details.errorCorrection: Substituting zero for absence confuses an awarded zero with an unanswered timeout.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Score presence and attempt status answer different questions. Zero is a completed score; timeout before any answer has no score and is labeled by status.
details.scenarioApplication: The exercise history must record both the numeric result when awarded and the separate reason an attempt has no score.
details.transfer: Keep an optional measurement separate from lifecycle state that explains why the measurement is absent.

messages.text: Optionality expresses whether a score exists; it does not redefine numeric zero.
The proposed encoding reverses the valid and absent cases.
Changing zero invents a score the policy did not award.
The status field already records why scoring did not occur.

feedback.reason: Zero is a valid score; absent score alone does not explain why no score exists, so timeout status remains separate.

options.text: Drop timeout status and infer it from the absent score.
Keep score optional; zero is a score, while timeout status explains absence.
Use zero for both a zero-point result and no score.
Use null for zero and a numeric score for unanswered attempts.
Store a score only after replacing zero with a minimum positive value.

questions.prompt: In a music practice tracker, the learner must complete a timed exercise. Completion records the exercise version and score policy. A completed timed attempt can score zero. A timeout before any answer produces no score and a separate timeout status. How should the score field be represented?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A consumer that needs only “may proceed” can derive that projection after receiving the richer result; it should not erase status at the query boundary.
details.errorCorrection: Null or false cannot distinguish an awaiting review from a final rejection, and a service outage cannot establish pending.
details.mechanismOrProperty: Pending, rejected, and approved are states of an existing request. Not-found means no request exists, while query failure means its state was not established.
details.scenarioApplication: A boolean can project whether approval is sufficient, but the authoritative query must preserve lifecycle state, request existence, and ability to read it.
details.transfer: Preserve the source status before deriving a simpler caller-facing decision.

messages.text: A boolean loses the distinction between awaiting review and a final rejection.
Null cannot represent all named states and still explain absence.
No request is not a rejection of an existing request.
An unavailable service does not prove the request is pending.

feedback.reason: Pending, rejected, approved, absent, and unreadable are different facts and may trigger different caller actions.

options.text: Return false for pending and rejected, and true for approved.
Return null for every state except approved.
Return “rejected” when no request ID is found.
Return “pending” when the approval service is unavailable.
Return request states, not-found, and query failure as distinct outcomes.

questions.prompt: In a procurement approval queue, the purchasing manager must approve an exception. Approval is attributable, bounded, and cannot bypass required controls. An exception request can be awaiting review, rejected, or approved. A missing request ID means no request exists; service failure means the state could not be read. How should a status query represent the results?

details.boundaryOrTradeoff: This is the authored profile-update contract. It does not claim all APIs assign these meanings to omitted or null fields.
details.errorCorrection: Using only a nullable string loses the difference between omitted and explicit null unless presence is preserved separately; treating either as an empty string also invents a supplied value.
details.mechanismOrProperty: A partial update needs to preserve field presence separately from its nullable content: omission, explicit null, and a supplied string are three different command intents in this prompt.
details.scenarioApplication: The handler leaves the existing note untouched for omission, clears it for null, and replaces it for a string; the parser must not erase which case arrived.
details.transfer: For partial updates, preserve the caller’s stated intent for each field instead of treating absence, clearing, and replacement as one nullable value.

messages.text: An empty string is a supplied value, not the stated meaning of omission or explicit null.
Omission means keep the current note under this contract, not replace it with a default.
This clears the note on omission even though omission means leave the current value unchanged.
This keeps the note on explicit null even though null means clear it.

feedback.reason: The operation assigns three different meanings to omitted, null, and string input; collapsing them would either clear, retain, or invent a value contrary to the request.

familyConfig.brief: Model the domain for a library loan service. A member may borrow eligible copies, return or renew a loan, and incur a hold when no copy is available. The system must preserve loan limits and prevent the same physical copy from being actively loaned twice. Describe behavior and ownership without assuming a particular language or persistence technology.

reviewCriteria.description: Clarify member eligibility, copy availability, renewal rules, holds, and the invariants that must always hold.
Assign state and behavior to domain concepts and explain the collaboration for borrow, return, and renewal.
Discuss invariant ownership, concurrency, extension points, and the cost of alternative responsibility boundaries.
Summarize the core model, protected invariants, major tradeoffs, and a useful validation step.

levels.description: Important goals, users, constraints, or assumptions are missing or contradictory.
levels.label: Unclear

levels.description: Some goals and constraints are named, but key ambiguities remain unresolved.
levels.label: Partial

levels.description: The main goals, constraints, assumptions, and open questions are stated clearly.
levels.label: Coherent

levels.description: Priorities, measurable constraints, assumptions, and follow-up questions are separated and traceable.
levels.label: Well bounded

levels.description: The proposed parts and their responsibilities or interactions cannot be followed.
levels.label: Unclear

levels.description: Some parts are identified, but important ownership or data-flow boundaries are absent.
levels.label: Partial

levels.description: Major responsibilities, boundaries, and flows connect to the stated requirements.
levels.label: Coherent

levels.description: The design makes ownership and critical flows explicit and relates them to constraints.
levels.label: Traceable

levels.description: Choices are asserted without naming costs, constraints, or alternatives.
levels.label: Unclear

levels.description: A benefit or cost is named, but the decision is weakly tied to the case constraints.
levels.label: Partial

levels.description: The main choice, its cost, and a relevant alternative are tied to stated constraints.
levels.label: Reasoned

levels.description: The decision boundary, rejected alternative, consequences, and conditions for revisiting it are clear.
levels.label: Explicit

levels.description: The response omits a stage or does not provide a usable conclusion.
levels.label: Incomplete

levels.description: All stages have a response, but the final summary leaves important decisions implicit.
levels.label: Partial

levels.description: The final response summarizes requirements, architecture, and key tradeoffs.
levels.label: Complete

levels.description: The final response connects decisions to priorities, risks, and the next validation step.
levels.label: Integrated
